--- title: "Labels, titles and annotation" --- ::: {.callout-tip} #### Learning objectives - Write headline titles, subtitles and captions. - Replace legends with direct labels. - Add annotations that explain the data. - Remove clutter with themes, and build a reusable theme of your own. ::: ::: {.before-after}
Legend ![](images/legend_lines.png) The eye goes line, legend, colour, line, for every line.
Direct labels ![](images/direct_labels.png) Each line is named where it ends.
::: ## Load packages and data ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder_2010.csv") gap_years <- read_csv("data/gapminder_1960_2010.csv") ``` ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd from plotnine import * gapminder = pd.read_csv("data/gapminder_2010.csv") gap_years = pd.read_csv("data/gapminder_1960_2010.csv") ``` ::: ::: ## Titles that say something Core `labs()` sets the title, subtitle, caption and axis labels in one place. - **Title**: the headline. What should the reader notice? - **Subtitle**: what is measured, where and when. - **Caption**: the source, and any notes on method. - **Axis labels**: plain words with units, never raw variable names. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(gapminder, aes(x = children_per_woman, y = life_expectancy)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + labs(title = "Where families are smaller, people live longer", subtitle = "167 countries, 2010", caption = "Source: Gapminder", x = "Children per woman", y = "Life expectancy (years)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} p = (ggplot(gapminder, aes(x="children_per_woman", y="life_expectancy")) + geom_point(alpha=0.6) + labs(title="Where families are smaller, people live longer", subtitle="167 countries, 2010", caption="Source: Gapminder", x="Children per woman", y="Life expectancy (years)") + theme(figure_size=(7, 4.4))) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} #### Titles in papers Journals usually want the headline in the figure legend rather than on the figure. The principle is the same: the first sentence of the legend should state the message. For talks and posters, put the headline on the figure itself. ::: ## Direct labels instead of legends Core For line charts, labelling each line where it ends removes the need for a legend. The approach is the same in both languages: make a small table of the last point of each line, then draw text there. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region_years <- gap_years |> group_by(region, year) |> summarise(life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") line_ends <- region_years |> filter(year == max(year)) ggplot(region_years, aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, colour = region)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_text(data = line_ends, aes(label = region), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1.5, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1960, 2010, 10), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.45))) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-3.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} region_years = (gap_years .groupby(["region", "year"], as_index=False)["life_expectancy"] .mean()) line_ends = region_years[region_years["year"] == region_years["year"].max()] p = (ggplot(region_years, aes(x="year", y="life_expectancy", color="region")) + geom_line(size=1.1) + geom_text(line_ends, aes(label="region"), ha="left", nudge_x=1.5, size=10, fontweight="bold") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=range(1960, 2011, 10), limits=(1960, 2035)) + labs(x="", y="Mean life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend_position="none", figure_size=(7, 4.4))) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: We extended the x axis to make room for the labels. Some labels may overlap where lines end close together. You can nudge individual labels by hand, or in R use the ggrepel package (`geom_text_repel()`), which moves labels apart automatically. ## Annotation Core Annotations explain *why* the data looks the way it does. `annotate()` adds a single piece of text, a line or a shape at a position you choose. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rwanda <- gap_years |> filter(country == "Rwanda") ggplot(rwanda, aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.1, colour = "#003E72") + annotate("segment", x = 1985, xend = 1993.5, y = 25, yend = 15, colour = "grey40", arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm"))) + annotate("text", x = 1984, y = 26, label = "1994 genocide", hjust = 1, colour = "grey30") + labs(title = "Rwanda: life expectancy collapsed in 1994 and then recovered", x = NULL, y = "Life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-3.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} rwanda = gap_years[gap_years["country"] == "Rwanda"] p = (ggplot(rwanda, aes(x="year", y="life_expectancy")) + geom_line(size=1.1, color="#003E72") + annotate("segment", x=1985, xend=1993.5, y=25, yend=15, color="#666666", arrow=arrow(length=0.08)) + annotate("text", x=1984, y=26, label="1994 genocide", ha="right", color="#4D4D4D") + labs(title="Rwanda: life expectancy collapsed in 1994 and then recovered", x="", y="Life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() + theme(figure_size=(7, 3.8))) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ## Themes and clutter Core Everything that is not data (grid lines, borders, backgrounds) should earn its place. Built-in themes such as `theme_minimal()` and `theme_classic()` are a good start. `theme()` controls individual elements; `element_blank()` removes one. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region_le <- gapminder |> group_by(region) |> summarise(life_expectancy = mean(life_expectancy)) ggplot(region_le, aes(x = life_expectancy, y = fct_reorder(region, life_expectancy))) + geom_col(fill = "grey70") + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) + labs(x = "Mean life expectancy (years)", y = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-3.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} region_le = gapminder.groupby("region", as_index=False)["life_expectancy"].mean() order = region_le.sort_values("life_expectancy")["region"] region_le["region"] = pd.Categorical(region_le["region"], categories=order) p = (ggplot(region_le, aes(x="region", y="life_expectancy")) + geom_col(fill="#B3B3B3") + coord_flip() + theme_minimal(base_size=13) + theme(panel_grid_major_y=element_blank(), panel_grid_minor=element_blank(), figure_size=(7, 3.6)) + labs(x="", y="Mean life expectancy (years)")) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: With `coord_flip()` in Python, the grid lines we removed are the ones that run along the bars. Try changing `panel_grid_major_y` to `panel_grid_major_x` to see the difference. ## Worked example: the full makeover Core Here are all the techniques from this part of the course in one figure: sort, grey, highlight, label directly, and write a headline. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} region_le |> mutate(focus = region == "Sub-Saharan Africa") |> ggplot(aes(x = life_expectancy, y = fct_reorder(region, life_expectancy), fill = focus)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", life_expectancy)), hjust = 1.2, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") + scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey65", "#D6083B"), guide = "none") + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) + labs(title = "Sub-Saharan Africa trails every other region by over 10 years", subtitle = "Mean life expectancy at birth across countries, 2010", caption = "Source: Gapminder", x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-3.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} region_le["focus"] = region_le["region"] == "Sub-Saharan Africa" region_le["label"] = region_le["life_expectancy"].map("{:.1f}".format) p = (ggplot(region_le, aes(x="region", y="life_expectancy", fill="focus")) + geom_col(width=0.7) + geom_text(aes(label="label"), ha="right", nudge_y=-1, color="white", fontweight="bold") + coord_flip() + scale_fill_manual(values=["#A6A6A6", "#D6083B"], guide=None) + scale_y_continuous(expand=(0, 0)) + labs(title="Sub-Saharan Africa trails every other region by over 10 years", subtitle="Mean life expectancy at birth across countries, 2010", caption="Source: Gapminder", x="", y="") + theme_minimal(base_size=13) + theme(panel_grid=element_blank(), axis_text_x=element_blank(), plot_title=element_text(size=13, weight="bold"), figure_size=(7, 3.8))) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: Because the values are written on the bars, the x axis is no longer needed, so we removed its text. ## Your own theme Extension If you make many figures, for a thesis or a paper, define your theme once and reuse it. Every figure will then look consistent. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} theme_mine <- function(base_size = 13) { theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), plot.title.position = "plot", legend.position = "top") } # then add + theme_mine() to any plot, or set it for the whole session: theme_set(theme_mine()) ``` ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} def theme_mine(base_size=13): return (theme_minimal(base_size=base_size) + theme(panel_grid_minor=element_blank(), plot_title=element_text(weight="bold"), legend_position="top")) # then add + theme_mine() to any plot, or set it for the whole session: theme_set(theme_mine()) ``` ::: ::: ## Exercises ::: {.callout-exercise} #### Write the labels {{< level 1 >}} Take any plot from an earlier chapter and give it a headline title, a subtitle, a caption with the source, and axis labels in plain words with units. ::: {.callout-answer collapse="true"} There is no single right answer. Check your title by asking: does it tell the reader what to notice, or only what is plotted? "Income and life expectancy" is a label. "Richer countries live longer, but the gains shrink at the top" is a headline. ::: ::: ::: {.callout-exercise} #### Label the lines {{< level 2 >}} Plot life expectancy over time for Brazil, India, Rwanda and the United Kingdom, with direct labels at the end of each line and no legend. ::: {.callout-answer collapse="true"} ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} four <- gap_years |> filter(country %in% c("Brazil", "India", "Rwanda", "United Kingdom")) ends <- four |> filter(year == max(year)) ggplot(four, aes(x = year, y = life_expectancy, colour = country)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = country), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1, fontface = "bold") + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.25))) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} four = gap_years[gap_years["country"].isin(["Brazil", "India", "Rwanda", "United Kingdom"])] ends = four[four["year"] == four["year"].max()] p = (ggplot(four, aes(x="year", y="life_expectancy", color="country")) + geom_line(size=1.1) + geom_text(ends, aes(label="country"), ha="left", nudge_x=1, fontweight="bold") + scale_x_continuous(limits=(1960, 2025)) + labs(x="", y="Life expectancy (years)") + theme_minimal() + theme(legend_position="none", figure_size=(7, 3.8))) p.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](labels-and-annotation_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-exercise} #### Annotate an event Extension {{< level 3 >}} Find another country with a sharp change in life expectancy (try Cambodia or Haiti). Plot it, and add an annotation that explains the event. ::: {.callout-answer collapse="true"} Cambodia shows a severe fall in the late 1970s, during the Khmer Rouge regime. Haiti shows a sharp fall in 2010, the year of the earthquake. Use `annotate("text", ...)` for the label and `annotate("segment", ...)` with an arrow to point at the event, as in the Rwanda example. ::: ::: ## Summary ::: {.callout-tip} #### Key points - The title is a headline; the subtitle says what is measured; the caption gives the source. - Use plain-language axis labels with units. - Direct labels are usually better than legends. - Annotations explain why the data looks the way it does. - Remove non-data elements that do not help, and reuse a theme for consistency. :::
